name: Soave

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

terms: Denominazione di Origine Controllata. The label names a precise area, and the wine is tested during production.
The original heartland of an Italian wine area.
keyfacts: Garganega is the principal grape, and Soave must contain a minimum of 70% Garganega.
Soave Superiore became a DOCG by decree of 29 October 2001, and Recioto di Soave received its own DOCG in 1998.
Soave Classico comes from part of the communes of Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone; Soave's soils are mostly volcanic, from decomposed basalt, with significant limestone outcrops.
Recioto di Soave uses the appassimento drying process and keeps much of its sweetness.
Soave Superiore Riserva needs a minimum alcohol of 12.5% and cannot be released before 1 November of the year after the harvest.

notes: Soave is a dry white, mainly from Garganega.
Classic Soave is medium bodied with a distinct bitter almond note, and some today is light, pale and fresh.
In the Classico zone, Garganega can give delicate wines with lemon, almond and spice.

blurb.text: A dry white wine from the Veneto, made around Verona, with Garganega as the principal grape. Most is dry and still and some is sparkling, while sweet Recioto di Soave has its own DOCG.
